title: LSP: Fix loading scene for every request on script file for workspace completion
body:
Fixes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/100934

Supersedes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/101091

I originally was only going to fix up some style issues to get the PR ready for merge, but ended up with some structure changes that I did not want to push to the original PR. (CC @dekaravanhoc if you are fine with the changes and want to integrate them feel free to do so!)

Differences:
- rebased onto recent LSP changes
- removed some excessive includes
- moved the scene cache into it's own file
- renamed some methods and parameters -> most of this is pretty subjective, some of it is meant to disambiguate or align stuff with other code
- adjusted the behaviour of `get` to do a blocking load as fallback -> this is a measure for edge cases when multiple clients are connected and was an easier solution for the edge case than refcounting the loaded instances.
- flattened out the additional queue struct. It made the code more clear but made the adjustment to `get` more complicated than necessary.

---

### Short explanation

GDScript autocompletion can provide certain options that are tied to a specific scene instance, e.g. node paths for `$Node` literals. In the builtin editor the opened scene is used for that so an instance is inherently present. For external editors we need a different approach. Previously we would search a scene, load it and instantiate it for every request from the external editor. This has shown to be too slow in certain situations.

This change introduces a cache that keeps those scene instances alive between requests.

+#pragma once

+#include "core/string/ustring.h"
+#include "core/templates/hash_map.h"
+#include "core/templates/local_vector.h"
+
+class Node;
+class EditorFileSystemDirectory;
+class PackedScene;
+
+/**
+ * Used to load and cache scene instances for LSP autocompletion.
+ *
+ * This implementation is not thread safe.
+ */
+class SceneCache {
+	// Always contains the path to the scene which is currently loaded via the `ResourceLoader`.
+	// If this is not empty, `script_path_queue` must have at least one element.
+	String current_loaded_owner;
+	LocalVector<String> script_path_queue;
+
+	HashMap<String, Node *> cache;
+
+	void _get_owner_paths(EditorFileSystemDirectory *p_dir, const String &p_script_path, LocalVector<String> &r_owner_paths);
+	void _finalize_scene_load();
+
+public:
+	void poll();
+
+	void clear();
+	void request_load(const String &p_script_path);
+	void unload(const String &p_script_path);
+
+	Node *get(const String &p_script_path);
+};
